title: Regular morphisms characterized on affine coordinate rings
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Then $f$ is regular [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] if and only if for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ and affine open $V\subseteq Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, the homomorphism $\varphi_{U,V}:\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$, obtained from the structure-sheaf map of $f$ followed by restriction to $U$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Tag 07R8, lemma-regular, equivalence (2) iff (3). The locally Noetherian source makes its fibre charts Noetherian. Its proof uses Varieties Tag 038V, lemma-geometrically-regular, in varieties.tex for the scheme/algebra comparison.

proof.text: Fix affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$. For $y\in V$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset A$, identify $\kappa(y)$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ compatibly with the map from $A$. The open fibre-product lemma identifies $U_y=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ with the inverse image of $U$ in $X_y$; the affine fibre-product formula identifies it, over $\kappa(y)$, with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. These opens cover $X_y$: choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ and cover $f^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $U$. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, $B$ is Noetherian, and the fibre-ring lemma makes each such tensor ring Noetherian. Thus $X_y$ is locally Noetherian by its affine open covering.

source.place: Tag 07R8, lemma-regular; affine fibre identifications and the locally Noetherian fibre hypothesis

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is regular. Its defining conditions give flatness and regularity of $(X_y)_K$ for every finite extension $K/\kappa(y)$. The flat-morphism affine criterion makes $A\to B$ flat. Apply the geometric-regularity affine-cover comparison, (1) => (2), to the locally Noetherian scheme $X_y$ and its affine open $U_y$ from step 1. It gives geometric regularity over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every $\mathfrak p$. Flatness together with these Noetherian geometrically regular fibre rings is exactly regularity of $A\to B$. The pair $(U,V)$ was arbitrary.

Conversely suppose every $\varphi_{U,V}$ is regular. The definition of a regular ring map makes all these maps flat, so the flat-morphism affine criterion gives flatness of $f$. Fix $y\in Y$. The affine opens $U_y$ constructed in step 1 cover $X_y$, and their coordinate rings $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are geometrically regular by the regularity of $A\to B$. Apply the geometric-regularity affine-cover comparison, (3) => (1), to $X_y$. It says that $(X_y)_K$ is regular for every finite extension $K/\kappa(y)$. As $y$ was arbitrary, these fibre conditions and flatness give regularity of $f$ by its definition.
